source_paper.title: Transient rapamycin treatment can increase lifespan and healthspan in middle-aged mice

population: middle-aged C57BL/6 mice (20 months at start)
intervention: transient rapamycin (8 mg/kg/day i.p.) for 3 months
canonical_phrase: 3 months of rapamycin extended remaining lifespan by ~60% in middle-aged mice
source_excerpt: 3 months of rapamycin treatment is sufficient to increase life expectancy by up to 60% and improve measures of healthspan in middle-aged mice.
notes: Source-verified 2026-05-14 via PMC4996648. The 60% figure is post-treatment life expectancy (from end of treatment forward); the same paper also reports 14-16% overall median lifespan from birth — those are NOT the same metric. Females (n.b.) did NOT extend at 8 mg/kg/day (p=0.261).

source_paper.title: mTOR inhibition improves immune function in the elderly

intervention: RAD001 (everolimus) 0.5 mg daily, 5 mg weekly, or 20 mg weekly for 6 weeks before vaccination
canonical_phrase: RAD001 improved influenza vaccine response by ~20% in the elderly
source_excerpt: RAD001 enhanced the response to the influenza vaccine by about 20% at doses that were relatively well tolerated.
notes: Source-verified 2026-05-14 via PubMed 25540326 abstract. Value 'about 20%' is the abstract's headline; per-arm best-responder details (0.5 mg daily / 5 mg weekly) live in the full text.

source_paper.title: Rapamycin-mediated lifespan increase in mice is dose and sex dependent and metabolically distinct from dietary restriction

intervention: encapsulated rapamycin in feed at 42 ppm (3x standard ITP dose)
canonical_phrase: rapamycin at 42 ppm extended male median lifespan by 23%
source_excerpt: The highest tested rapamycin dose increased median lifespan by 23% in males and 26% in females.
notes: Source-verified 2026-05-14 via PMC4032600 full text. Value matches abstract verbatim. Dose-response replication of Harrison 2009 across 4.7 / 14 / 42 ppm.
